title: A curve modification cannot contract an isolated whole fibre component
statement: Let $T$ be integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and Noetherian (admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Let $X\to T$ and $Y\to T$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]) morphisms with pure one-dimensional geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] (every irreducible component has topological Krull dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]). Assume that the generic fibre $X_\eta$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and that every geometric fibre of $Y/T$ is nodal: its nonsmooth points have completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field (completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], power series [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]). Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper $T$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], an isomorphism on the generic fibre and between schematically dense open subschemes; schematically dense means that $\mathcal O\to j_*\mathcal O$ is injective for the open inclusion $j$. For any geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, no nonempty connected component $W$ of $Y_\Omega$ which is proper over $\Omega$ is mapped by $f_\Omega$ to a single point of $X_\Omega$. In particular a proper irreducible component disjoint from every other irreducible component of $Y_\Omega$ cannot be contracted. No marking or stability assumption is imposed, and neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed separated or proper over $T$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 1.1, p. 3, the non-isolated contracted-subcurve input implicit in the stable pointed-subcurve argument. Auxiliary geometric statement extracted by Q83; its usual proof uses source-local Stein factorization (Stacks more-morphisms.tex Tag 03H0, theorem-stein-factorization-Noetherian).

proof.text: Suppose that a component W as in the statement is mapped to a point x, and write s for the image of Spec Omega in T. The geometric fibre Y_Omega is Noetherian by finite-type base change and the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma. Its finitely many irreducible components cover it. Group these components by chains of nonempty intersections: the union in each group is connected and closed, and its complement is the union of the other finitely many groups, hence closed. These groups are exactly the connected components. Consequently W is an open-and-closed subscheme. It has a closed point w by quasi-compactness and the Kolmogorov property of a scheme. Since W is of finite type over the algebraically closed field Omega, kappa(w)=Omega; its image gives an Omega-rational point x of X_Omega. If s=eta, f_Omega is an isomorphism and W contains an entire one-dimensional irreducible component, so its image cannot be a point. Hence s is distinct from eta.

source.place: Noetherian finite-component topology; closed point and rational residue-field argument (agent deduction from the cited nodes).

proof.text: Apply the Noetherian specialization-trait lemma to eta specializing to s in T. It supplies a DVR R and a:Spec R -> T with closed point r mapping to s and generic point mapping to eta. Put K=Frac(R), X_R=X times_T Spec R, Y_R=Y times_T Spec R, and f_R=f times_T Spec R. The map on generic fibres is an isomorphism. The definition of a DVR makes R a Noetherian local PID, a valuation ring, and a domain; fix a nonzero uniformizer pi.

Choose a common extension M of Omega and kappa(r) over kappa(s), then an algebraic closure L of M. Thus the closed geometric fibre of Y_R over L identifies with Y_L=Y_Omega times_Omega L. Let W_L be the inverse image of W; it is open and closed. It is nonempty: a point of W with residue field E lifts after choosing a common extension of E and L over Omega. Its image under f_L is the single L-rational point x_L. Here this assertion does not presume schematic constancy or reducedness: in an affine neighbourhood of x, every function in the maximal ideal of x pulls back on each affine of W to a nilpotent (it belongs to every prime). After scalar extension these functions are still nilpotent, so the image is contained in the base change of the rational point x; that base change has one point. Nonemptiness gives equality.

source.place: Tag 0H7K, lemma-common-extension-field, and Tag 09GT; elementary nilradical argument for the image under field extension.

proof.text: The morphisms X_R -> Spec R and Y_R -> Spec R are of finite type by finite-type base change. They are flat: on an affine base-change chart, if C is flat over A, then C tensor_A R is flat over R, since for an injection N1 -> N2 of R-modules, Ni tensor_R (R tensor_A C) identifies with Ni tensor_A C and the latter injection follows from flatness of C. Apply the affine criterion, including localization on the charts. Restriction to an open preserves the same criterion. This verifies flatness without any regularity, excellence, or separatedness assumption on T.

source.place: Tag 01U5, affine criterion; elementary tensor argument proving base-change flatness (Tag 01U9).

proof.text: Let x0 be the image of x_L in X_R. Choose an affine open U=Spec A of X_R containing x0 and put V=f_R^{-1}(U). The entire W_L lies in V_L. Properness is preserved first under the base change T <- Spec R and then under the open base change U -> X_R, so V -> U is proper. Since X_R is of finite type over the Noetherian affine Spec R, X_R is Noetherian; its affine open U is Noetherian and of finite type over R (all its opens are quasi-compact). The proper finite-type scheme V over U is Noetherian. In particular V is quasi-compact and quasi-separated as a scheme: every intersection of affine opens is an open subset of its Noetherian underlying space and is therefore quasi-compact.

source.place: Properness under arbitrary base change, Tag 01W6; finite-type composition and Noetherian affine-local reduction.

proof.text: Put B=Gamma(V,O_V) and take the affine Stein factorization V --q--> Z=Spec B --h--> U. The affine Stein theorem says that q is proper with geometrically connected, nonempty fibres. Since V is locally Noetherian, O_V is coherent: it is quasi-coherent of finite type. Proper coherent cohomology over the Noetherian ring A, in degree zero, now says that B is a finite A-module. Thus h is finite by the definition of a finite morphism. In particular B is a finite-type R-algebra and Z is Noetherian. This use of coherent cohomology is over U, not over Spec R; V need not be proper over Spec R.

The R-module B is torsion free. Indeed, for any affine chart V_i=Spec C_i of V, flatness of V/R and the affine criterion make C_i flat over R. For 0 != b in R, tensor the injection R --b--> R with C_i: multiplication by b on C_i is injective. If b z=0 for a global section z in B, its restriction to every V_i is therefore zero, hence z=0 by the sheaf condition. Since R is a valuation ring, the torsion-free-module-flat lemma of this unit applies to B. The affine criterion gives flatness of Z -> Spec R.

source.place: Tag 0539 (valuation-ring case); torsion-freeness is the displayed affine-chart argument using the definition of flatness.

proof.text: Because V is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, flat base change of global sections along Spec K -> Spec R gives B tensor_R K = Gamma(V_K,O). The localization R -> K is flat: apply the localization-preserves-flatness lemma to the free rank-one R-module R. The generic isomorphism f_K identifies V_K with U_K, which is affine (U_K=Spec(A tensor_R K)). Therefore h_K:Z_K -> U_K is an isomorphism, with the canonical ring identification above. No assertion of global-sections base change along the nonflat closed-fibre map R -> L is used.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, degree zero; generic localization only.

proof.text: The generic fibre Z_K is pure of dimension one. To check this precisely over K, take an algebraic closure Kbar. The scheme X_Kbar is a geometric fibre of X/T, hence every irreducible component has dimension one. Its local topological dimension is one everywhere by the equidimensional-open lemma with O=X_Kbar. Each point of X_K lifts after field extension (the common-extension-fields argument applied to its residue field). On affine charts, invariance of local topological dimension under field extension therefore gives dimension one at every point of X_K. Local topological dimension is unchanged on an open neighbourhood, directly from its definition. Thus it is one throughout U_K. The constant-local-dimension-components lemma, applied to this locally Noetherian open, makes U_K pure one-dimensional. Transfer this along the isomorphism Z_K=U_K from Step 8.

source.place: Tag 0A21; local dimension under field extension and the constant-local-dimension criterion in the cited nodes.

proof.text: The generic fibre Z_K=D(pi) is dense in Z. Indeed, if a basic open D(b) is disjoint from D(pi), then b pi belongs to every prime, so (b pi)^n=0 for some n. Torsion-freeness of B over the domain R implies b^n=0, hence D(b) is empty. Now apply the flat-dense-generic-fibre pure-dimension lemma to Z -> Spec R, with d=1. Its base is integral, it is flat by Step 7 and locally of finite type by Step 6, and Steps 9 and this paragraph verify its generic-fibre hypotheses. In particular the geometric closed fibre Z_L is pure one-dimensional.

source.place: Tag 0GSK, remark-flat-equidimensional, second list with F=O_Z; density proved by the elementary nilradical argument.

proof.text: Base change q to L. Its fibres remain connected and nonempty, and q_L is proper and hence closed. A connected fibre meets at most one of the disjoint clopen subsets W_L and V_L minus W_L. Consequently F=q_L(W_L) satisfies q_L^{-1}(F)=W_L. Surjectivity implies q_L(V_L minus W_L)=Z_L minus F. Both images are closed, so F is a nonempty clopen subset of Z_L. Since h_L q_L=f_L, we have h_L(F)={x_L}. The finite morphism h remains finite after this affine base change: if B is generated by b1,...,bn as an A-module, their tensors generate B tensor_R L as an A tensor_R L-module. Thus its fibre over x_L is finite.

source.place: Tag 03H2; elementary saturation of a clopen under a closed surjection with connected fibres. Finite affine base change is the displayed module-generator argument.

proof.text: Every point in h_L^{-1}(x_L) is closed in Z_L. In fact x_L is an L-rational point in the affine U_L, hence is closed there, and its inverse image is the spectrum of a finite-dimensional L-algebra. The quotient by any prime is a finite-dimensional L-domain, hence a field by the cited lemma; its primes are therefore maximal. Thus the finite subset F is a finite discrete closed subset. Since F is also open in Z_L, each of its singleton subsets is open in Z_L and has local topological dimension zero. But Z_L is locally of finite type over L and pure one-dimensional by Step 10, so the equidimensional-open-local-dimension lemma says that its local topological dimension is one at every point. This contradicts F being nonempty.

source.place: Finite-dimensional-domain-is-field by multiplication and rank-nullity; varieties.tex Tag 0A21 for the contradiction.

proof.text: This contradiction excludes the assumed W. Finally, an irreducible component C of Y_Omega disjoint from every other irreducible component is closed, and its complement is the finite union of those other closed components. Hence C is open as well. It is nonempty and irreducible, therefore connected, and no connected subset can meet both C and its clopen complement. It is a connected component. If C is proper, the assertion just proved excludes its contraction. This proves both conclusions with the original hypotheses; smoothness, nodality, schematic density, and properness of W were not needed beyond the finite-type hypotheses used above.

source.place: Tag 004W and finite-component topology; elementary final implication.
